item.title: Anchors Adrift? Old and New Anchor Organizations, Structural Change, and the Transfer of Knowledge to the Wider Economy
item.content:encoded:
Martin Andersson, Blekinge Institute of Technology

Pontus Braunerhjelm, KTH Royal Institute of Technology

Anders Broström, KTH Royal Institute of Technology

Albert N. Link, University of North Carolina at Greensboro

This collection examines how anchor organizations—large multinational firms, universities, and research hospitals—generate knowledge spillovers and innovation in their regions. The traditional view holds that such anchors drive growth through spinoffs, labor mobility, and technology transfer. However, structural economic changes have transformed these dynamics: multinationals now operate globally with internalized venturing, new platform and software firms grow without proportional local employment, and digital technologies alter spillover patterns.

The collection invites research on how spillover mechanisms function under contemporary conditions across established anchors adapting to globalization, new firm types potentially replacing traditional anchors, universities maintaining their roles amid technological change, and whether digitalization and AI reshape geographically bounded knowledge transfer. Contributions should engage with transfer mechanisms explicitly rather than only documenting regional economic effects, and may address policy instruments like FDI attraction and cluster programs that may require updating to match new anchor realities.

Appel publié par The Journal of Technology Transfer. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.
